articles.title: Long-range hits and goals galore: inside the Premier League’s return to chaos | Andrew Beasley
articles.summary: Teams are running further and set-piece strikes are in decline as end-to-end football takes over the division. Goals in the Premier League are up. Chaos is returning. End-to-end football is back. The division is more open, in more ways than one.
body: The figures show a rise from 2.75 goals per game last season to 2.82 so far this year, which is a small average increase – but one that could easily widen. The goals-per-game rate was at least 0.21 higher across the final 330 games than it was for the first 50 in four of the past five seasons. If 2026-27 sees a similar upturn, it will become the second highest scoring season in the Premier League era.

Goals should be harder to come by at this time of year when teams are fresher, more organised and less ragged. Their legs haven’t yet been drained by the December fixture pile-up or the demands of European football. Evidence of this can be seen in every team averaging more distance per match than they did in 2025-26. Liverpool are bottom of the division for this metric yet are ahead of any club’s final figure from last season.
points: Teams are running further and set-piece strikes are in decline as end-to-end football takes over the division.

articles.title: Harry Brook says Brydon Carse ‘just needs time away from the international scene’
articles.summary: Captain says bowler ‘is working on a few things’ England v Sri Lanka ODIs come a year before World Cup. Harry Brook is hopeful that Brydon Carse will break back into his England white-ball teams once the fast bowler is clear of his ongoing disciplinary, describing him as a “very good mate” who is…
body: Carse has recently discovered he will not face a criminal charge for the late-night incident in Derby last month that led to him being briefly handcuffed. But while technically available for selection, the 31-year-old has not featured in England’s squads since that night as he awaits the outcome of an investigation by the Cricket Regulator.

Asked before Tuesday’s first one-day international against Sri Lanka at Chester-le-Street about the prospect of Carse returning down the line, Brook, England’s white-ball captain, replied: “He’s a very good cricketer. He’s been bowling extremely well for Durham. When his time for selection is up, that will be a debate.

“I’m very good mates with Carsey. I’ve spoken a lot with him. Those conversations are private. I think he just needs time away from the international scene. He’s working on a few things behind the scenes and hopefully he’ll be ready at some point in the future.”

More broadly, Brook believes the call for greater off-field professionalism has permeated through the England squads, both from Brendon McCullum, the white-ball head coach, and Stephen Fleming ahead of his new role with the Test side.

articles.title: The last two seasons were grim for Spurs. This is as bad as it’s ever been | Jonathan Wilson
articles.summary: Pre-season thoughts of European qualification are already beginning to look bafflingly optimistic for Roberto De Zerbi’s team. Sign up for our free newsletter here. In March, Tottenham, fearing possible relegation, spent big to bring in Roberto De Zerbi, who will probably never go into a…
body: To an extent, the issue is confidence. On the opening weekend at Brentford, with a weird mishmash of a side, a team that was clearly undercooked, they were hammered 3-0 by much better-prepared opponents. That was not hugely surprising given how sensible Brentford’s transfer dealing had been and how early they had done it. More worrying was what happened the following week as Spurs, starting well before fading, lost 2-0 at home to Newcastle.

Goalless draws against Nottingham Forest and Everton seemed to have steadied the ship. Their biggest problem seemed to be a lack of confidence. They were tentative in possession, indecisive when chances did come. The two goals they managed in their 3-2 defeat to Aston Villa on Saturday mean Spurs climbed above Coventry to second-bottom of the goal-scoring charts, but they are ninth for shots. That should be reason for frustration rather than panic; the goals will come eventually.

articles.title: Pierre Sage took Lens to new heights. His replacement left after six games
articles.summary: Lens finished second in Ligue 1 last season and won the Coupe de France. Building on that success is proving tricky. By Get French Football News. It was under cover of darkness that Yannick Cahuzac took his place in the Lens dugout at the Stade Louis II on Friday night.
body: Cahuzac’s appointment, much like his entrance in Monaco, had a stealthy quality, as if he had always been there and the switching of the lights was mere confirmation of his presence. Cahuzac left Lorient, where he had been Olivier Pantaloni’s assistant, at the end of last season to return to Lens, where he had finished his playing career before working as Franck Haise’s assistant in the 2022–23 campaign.

He was spoken about as a future No 1, but that was not the role he took in the summer. Cahuzac is still an apprentice who has not yet obtained his coaching qualifications so he returned to the club as an assistant to Toppmöller. The German had the unenviable task of succeeding Pierre Sage, who hastily departed to Crystal Palace after guiding Lens to a maiden Coupe de France triumph and a second-place finish in Ligue 1 last season.

articles.title: Wales will have no fear in Portugal - James
articles.summary: Jordan James insists depleted Wales will not be overawed against "the best players in the world" in their Nations League A opener against Portugal on Thursday.
body: A Wales squad already missing the likes of Joe Rodon and Dylan Lawlor has been hit by the withdrawals of Karl Darlow, Nathan Broadhead and star man Harry Wilson.

Having returned to the top tier of the Nations League by winning their League B group in 2024, Wales begin what looks like being a demanding campaign as they meet a star-studded Portuguese side in Lisbon.
Portugal can call on a string of star names including Ruben Dias, Joao Cancelo, Nuno Mendes, Vitinha, Joao Neves and Bruno Fernandes, not to mention 41-year-old Cristiano Ronaldo.
But Wolverhampton Wanderers midfielder James says Wales will have "no fear" as they go in search of a first win since last November's World Cup qualifying triumph against North Macedonia.

articles.title: Lions tour a 'top goal' for Wales prop Tuipulotu
articles.summary: Wales prop Sisilia Tuipulotu says selection for next year's inaugural British and Irish Lions women's tour is among her top rugby priorities.
body: The in-form tight-head scored two tries in Wales' emphatic 50-19 victory over South Africa on Friday, under the watchful eye of Lions head coach Jo Yapp.
With Yapp saying she will only take the best players in each position, most of the touring party to New Zealand is expected to be made up of England's world cup-winning stars.
But Tuipulotu's barnstorming display certainly puts her on the radar for when the squad is announced in May.
"I actually didn't know she [Yapp] was there until after the game, but I'm very happy that we gave the performance that we did in front of her," said Tuipulotu.

articles.title: Avonte Maddox out for year, as Lions seek DB ‘shake up’
articles.summary: Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell delivered tough injury news on Monday, noting that veteran safety Avonte Maddox will miss the rest of the 2026 season after suffering a foot injury on Thursday night that will require surgery. “That hurts a little bit,” Campbell said.
body: "That hurts a little bit," Campbell said. "Maddox is a good player for us. Good solid football player, headsy. I hate that for him. But that's the hand that we're dealt, and we move forward."

Maddox was starting for the Lions at safety for the first two weeks of the season while Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch remain on the Physically Unable to Perform list. Both Joseph and Branch are eligible to return to practice this week, Campbell noted that both still need more time.

That leaves the Lions in a bit of a precarious spot at safety moving forward. Detroit has Chuck Clark and Thomas Harper capable of stepping in and starting, but the depth behind that only currently includes Christian Izien —who has been playing more nickel lately.

The Lions have reportedly been in search for some veteran safety help on the free agent market, and held a workout on Monday morning that reportedly included Jordan Fuller, Jalen Mills, and Mike Edwards, among others. Campbell noted that the search won't just be limited to available veterans, either.

articles.title: Scotland's Scott promoted to PGA Tour with Ohio win
articles.summary: Scotland's Sandy Scott puts a career-threatening wrist injury behind him to earn promotion to the main PGA Tour for the first time after winning the Nationwide Children's Hospital Championship in Columbus, Ohio.
body: The 28-year-old's one-stroke victory on Sunday was his first on the Korn Ferry Tour and lifted him to second spot on the development tour's points list.
It came a week after he finished runner-up at the Simmons Bank Open for the Snedeker Foundation in Franklin, Tennessee.
The native of Inverness needed two surgeries after tearing ligaments in his right wrist in 2019 and admitted: "I was in some really low times and didn't know if I'd ever play golf again."
Scott battled back from that but withdrew from this season's BMW Charity Pro-Am and missed two months of the season after the wrist flared up again.

articles.title: McLaren predict four-way battle for Baku win after confirming more upgrades
articles.summary: McLaren have confirmed they will bring more upgrades to this weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, where they are expecting a four-way battle for victory with Mercedes, Ferrari and Red Bull.
body: After failing to claim a victory in the first 10 grands prix of the season, the reigning constructors' champions have come into form, with Lando Norris claiming three pole positions at the last four races and only being denied a third win by the unfortunate timing of a virtual safety car last time out in Madrid.
McLaren have once more exhibited strength in development, with regular upgrades brought to the MCL40 having played a significant part in catapulting them back into contention for victories.

The team's official preview for this weekend's race in Baku, which takes place on Saturday rather than the usual Sunday slot, revealed there will be new parts, and that their rotating 'H-Wing' will return to the car after not being used in Madrid.
"As part of the team's continued journey throughout the 2026 season, the team will bring to Baku a set of upgrades aimed to improve the aerodynamic performance of the MCL40," the team said.

articles.title: Spurs bottom of PL but more than £300m spent - where do they go from here?
articles.summary: This time it was supposed to be different. After multiple false dawns for Tottenham Hotspur, the club had a manager with proven Premier League experience, and had handed him a £300m+ war chest - easily the biggest in its entire history.
body: Instead, Spurs find themselves bottom of the table after five games for the first time in 18 years, with their only goals a pair of consolation strikes on another dismal afternoon against Aston Villa at the weekend.

Things aren't quite as bad as the table suggests and had Tottenham taken any of a number of presentable first-half chances against Villa, they would have gone into the three-week international break silencing some of the noise around the club.
But instead, two points from five games and such a dismal record in front of goal has kept the spotlight firmly on them.

Though it is only five games, their struggles to find consistency have extended into a third consecutive season. Tottenham have now picked up just 18 points in 2026 and, since the start of 2024/25, still one fewer than a West Ham side who were relegated at the end of last season.

articles.summary: Captain Harry Brook says leaning on a mentor of Kevin Pietersen's calibre will only help the continued upward trajectory of England's white-ball sides.
body: Pietersen, regarded as one of the greatest batters of the 21st century, has been brought into the England white-ball set-up in a mentoring role by head coach Brendon McCullum in the build-up to next year's 50-over World Cup.

Brook shed light on the impact Pietersen was already having on the squad, both on and off the field, with the team's approach to playing spin already addressed in a masterclass from the former England captain.
"KP has been very good," Brook told a press conference. "He's enjoying the role, he's enjoying himself.
"He's been good to have around, little chats here and there. Away from the game, sat having a coffee and a chat about how he sees the game and how he thinks it should be played.
